newsitem.title: USA: Oregon Metallurgical sees lower golf sales.
newsitem.headline: Oregon Metallurgical sees lower golf sales.

text.p: ALBANY, Ore., March 7 (Oregon) - Oregon Metallurgical Corp said Friday it expects its sales to golf clubhead producers will be about $25 million lower in 1997 than they were in 1996.
The company said in a statement the lower revenue is due to inventory accumulation by the golf clubhead producers coupled with their increased efficiency in recycling internal scrap.

Oregon Metallurgical reported sales of $237 million in 1996 of which about $40 million was to the golf clubhead producers. The company said it expects sales to this industry will be about $15 million in 1997.
"While the lower demand in 1997 is disappointing, this is a temporary, not a permanent, loss since demand for titanium golf clubs continues to increase," the company said in a statement.
Oregon Metallurgical makes titanium sponge, ingot, mill products and castings for use in the aerospace, industrial, golf and military markets.
